NON-CONTINUOUS WERBS / STATIVE VERBS

Some English verbs aren't used in continuous
tenses. These verbs often describe states that

last for some time. A stative verb describes a

state rather than an action.

It is important to remember that non-continuous
verbs or stative verbs cannot be used in any
continuous tenses. Instead of using Present Perfect
Continuous with these verbs, we must use Present
Perfect.

She did not agree to take the medication.

It appears to be the result of previous SN
experiences with chemo that led to A)

nausea and vomiting.

NON-CONTINUOUS WERBS / STATIVE VERBS

1. Existing state/state: be, cost, fit, mean, suit,
seem,appear, depend, include, consist of, exist,
contain

2. Feelings/emotional states: hate, hope, like,
love, prefer,regret, want, wish, detest, envy,
dislike, mind, fear

3. Possession: belong, have, own, need

4. Sensory perception/senses: feel, hear, see,

www.honorsgroup.com

smell, taste, touch

5. Introductory clauses for direct

speech: answer, ask, reply, say

6.Brain work/thought/mental states: believe,
know,think, understand, assume, an
consider, suppose, expect, agree, aN

remember, forget, doubt, imagine

NON-CONTINUOUS WERBS / STATIVE VERBS

Some verbs can be both stative and non-stative:
be, have, think, taste, smell, think, consider, smell,
feel, look, see,etc.

be - be is usually a stative verb, but when it is
used in the continuous it means ‘behaving’ or
‘acting’.

forms of be : is, are, was, were, being;

He was anxious, She is being worried.

Have (stative) - own

www.honorsgroup.com

He has hypertension.
Have (non-stative) - part of an expression
Iam having a cup of tea.

See (stative) - see with eyes/understand
See (non-stative) - meet an
Think (stative) - have an opinion (fa

I think that she requires a nutritional assessment.

\

Think (Non-stative) - have in mind

lam thinking about my duty hours.
